title: Bootstrap CDK and create a GitHub deploy role in each chatticus-* account
description:
Ryan (2026-09-30): set up the same CI/CD in the new per-environment accounts: CI in GitHub Actions, CD by CDK deploy through GitHub OIDC. This card is the foundation and needs no DNS or data decisions.

## Findings (read-only, 2026-09-30)
- chatticus-development, -staging and -production are empty: no CDKToolkit stack, no OIDC provider, no stacks. Non-root SSO sessions (AdministratorAccess) work for all three.
- infra/lib/github-deploy-stack.ts cannot be reused as is: it IMPORTS the GitHub OIDC provider (fromOpenIdConnectProviderArn, which must already exist) and creates all three environment roles in ONE account. A new account needs the provider created and only its own environment's role.
- Trust is by the OIDC sub claim pinned to the repo's immutable owner/repo ids plus environment:NAME (see the long comment in that file); keep that, it was root-caused once already.
- The CDK account is chosen from the credentials (CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT in bin/chatticus.ts), so deploying to a different account needs no code change: a workflow's AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN environment secret decides where it deploys. That secret is therefore the cutover switch, not something to change early.

## Plan
1. cdk bootstrap aws://ACCOUNT/us-east-1 in each account (AGENTS.md allows bootstrap and deploy as the only AWS writes).
2. A stack that creates the OIDC provider (one per account) and ONE deploy role trusting environment:<that account's environment> only, with a test that asserts the trust, and the legacy stack left untouched until legacy is retired. Deploy it once per account locally with the SSO profile (the documented one-time path).
3. Do NOT change any AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN secret here; workflows keep deploying to legacy until the cutover card.

## Done when
In each account: CDKToolkit is CREATE_COMPLETE, the deploy role exists, and a dispatch of a no-op check (sts get-caller-identity through OIDC from GitHub Actions) succeeds without touching legacy.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Started 2026-09-30 (Ryan: start the bootstrap card). Approach: (1) cdk bootstrap each account with its non-root SSO profile, development first, verify, then staging and production; (2) code: a new ChatticusAccountDeploy stack reusing the existing createGithubDeployRole (exported) plus an OIDC provider created in the account, one role per account for its own environment, with a test of the trust; (3) a verify workflow (workflow_dispatch, role ARN as an input, NOT the AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN secret) that assumes the new role through real OIDC and prints the account, so no existing GitHub environment secret is changed and legacy keeps deploying to legacy. The stack is merged to develop before it is deployed, so deployed infra matches develop.

comments.author: home
comments.text: DONE 2026-09-30. (1) cdk bootstrap in chatticus-development, -staging, -production: CDKToolkit CREATE_COMPLETE, version 32 (same as legacy); legacy untouched. (2) #375 merged (133920e): ChatticusAccountDeploy, deployed once per account from Ryan's non-root SSO session with an account guard: one GitHub OIDC provider (audience sts.amazonaws.com) and ONE role chatticus-github-actions-deploy per account, trust pinned to the repository ids plus that account's own environment claim (verified by reading the deployed trust policies: development/staging/production each trust only their own), AdministratorAccess attached as in legacy, no IAM users or keys created, standard tags applied. (3) masked GitHub ENVIRONMENT secret AWS_NEW_ACCOUNT_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN set on development, staging and production; the live AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN secrets were NOT touched, so every existing workflow still deploys to legacy. (4) REAL OIDC verified from GitHub Actions for all three environments: role assumed, CDKToolkit CREATE_COMPLETE, zero 12-digit identifiers in the public logs. How it was verified: verify-account-deploy-role.yml is workflow_dispatch-only and GitHub only allows dispatching a workflow that exists on the default branch (main), which gets it only at the next develop-to-main release (that push also auto-deploys staging and production to legacy, so it was not forced). Instead a throwaway branch carried a push-triggered copy; both branches were deleted. After the next release the workflow can be dispatched as designed. FINDING filed separately: none of the three GitHub environments restricts which branches may use it.
